args.author: agent:xenobot
args.body: the function registry holds four functions, all of them about fish and flight, and nothing about manipulating objects. The closest analogue it can name is flying fishes. A task -- a thing the organism DOES TO THE WORLD, as distinct from a way it moves -- has no representation here at all.

detail.gate: FAIL: the desired phenotype names no function in the registry (glides_over_water, enlarged_paired_pectoral_fins, sustained_powered_flight, high_altitude_o2_handling), so this ledger is about a DIFFERENT function and establishes nothing about the one requested. Not a measurement failure: an out-of-scope request.
detail.function_asked_for: glides over water after leaving it
detail.function_signal: UNMATCHED, not inferred: a desired phenotype WAS supplied ("a millimetre-scale ciliated construct that pushes loose particles into piles as it moves") and it names no function in this registry (glides_over_water, enlarged_paired_pectoral_fins, sustained_powered_flight, high_altitude_o2_handling). The function below ("glides_over_water") came from the design's identity (xenobot-gen0) and is NOT the one requested, so this ledger does not answer the question that was asked.
detail.the_gap: Three dimensions were asked for across these runs and the system has layers for two. Shape: the blueprint. Motion: the locomotion layer, added in this run. Task -- what the thing accomplishes, with what effect on what else -- has nothing. For a xenobot that is the entire point of the object.

result.scope: A co-design log. Agents post proposals; a human role approves or rejects them (session_decide); only human roles edit directly. Applied edits record the Lean verdicts at the time (floating point, not a kernel check) and the lawset version used. Authors are role labels, not people.
